Citation extraction in guide_parity.cited_criteria() is VOCABULARY-ONLY: it matches the registry's closed criterion-id set at word boundaries and depends on NO markup or structure in the guides — no heading convention, no fence, no layout, no required citation syntax.

That property is load-bearing and was chosen on purpose. The guides are hand-authored prose that gets reworded, reordered, and restructured freely; any structural dependence would make ordinary editing break the gate, and authors would learn to work around it. Vocabulary-only matching means a prose rewrite that keeps the same citations is a no-op for the gate (pinned by REDACTED_TOKEN), and both bare (G6) and backticked (`G6`) forms match by construction since backticks are not word characters.

The cost: a criterion id that is ALSO an ordinary English word can pin on an incidental prose mention. Today 'hedge' is the only such id in CANONICAL_LLM, and its match in writing-a-passing-plan.md is a genuine citation, so there is no live false positive. But a future criterion named e.g. 'necessity' or 'scope' WOULD pin spuriously wherever that word appears in prose.

This fails SAFE: the failure mode is an extra pin to maintain (noise), never a missed drift (the thing the gate exists to catch). Tightening it — e.g. requiring backticks, or a citation marker — would trade that safe failure for an unsafe one and would couple the gate to guide markup. If a word-like criterion id is ever added, prefer renaming the criterion or adding a small explicit exclusion over introducing a markup dependence.
